title: On-prem compact usage bundler and deterministic quota reconciliation for delayed exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Customers running Redwood Private / VPC can be air-gapped or only intermittently connected. We currently produce per-request usage events but our on-prem collectors produce large, unshaped blobs which cause long upload times and make reconciliation with cloud billing and quota engines brittle when exports are delayed or retried.

Goal:
Replace the existing on-prem upload format with a compact, deterministic bundler and reconciliation algorithm that guarantees correct per-customer quota accounting and deterministic rate-limit state after applying delayed exports. Primary goals are: correctness (no double-charging or missed usage when exports are replayed), bounded memory and disk overhead on on-prem collectors, and deterministic ordering so cloud-side consumers can apply idempotent deltas.

High-level design:
- Compact bundler: collector will write time-windowed bundles (default window=10m) as newline-delimited compressed protobuf blobs (proto v2) with a small manifest. Each bundle contains: monotonic bundle_id (UUID v1), sequence_offset (monotonic per-customer sequence), per-route aggregated counters (tokens_consumed, tokens_blocked), and a small sampling of raw events for debugging (0.1% sampling). Bundles are signed locally with the node key to detect tampering during airgap transfer.
- Deterministic sequence IDs: each usage event gets a monotonic local sequence number; bundles record starting_sequence and ending_sequence. Cloud importer will apply bundles in sequence_number order and skip already-applied sequence ranges to achieve idempotency.
- Compact delta model: instead of shipping raw events, the collector will compute per-bucket deltas for counters (per-model/per-route) within the bundle to reduce size and make reconciliation O(aggregates) not O(events).
- Local quota enforcement: On-prem runtime continues enforcing rate limits using local token buckets. Each quota enforcement point records tokens_granted and tokens_rejected in the bundle. During reconciliation we treat tokens_rejected as enforcement decisions that must be replayed to preserve customer-facing behavior and to reconcile metrics.
- Reconciliation algorithm: Cloud importer maintains per-customer watermark (highest_applied_sequence). Incoming bundle with starting_sequence > watermark+1 indicates missing data; importer will mark customer export as "incomplete" and queue a reconciliation job. When overlapping bundles arrive (retries), importer applies only the delta for sequences not yet applied and compares resulting counters against post-apply invariants (total_tokens_consumed >= 0, tokens_granted+tokens_rejected == attempts). Discrepancies trigger automated audit alerts and optional human review.
- Offline conflict resolution: If two collectors generate overlapping sequence ranges (split-brain) we resolve deterministically by node_id ordering (lower node_id wins for overlapping sequences) and emit a correction delta to zero out the duplicate counts in the later-applied bundle.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- No billing-impacting reconciliation incidents in 30 days during a staged rollout to 5 pilot customers.
- Bundle size reduced by >= 6x vs current opaque blob for a representative traffic sample.
- Cloud importer idempotency: applying the same bundle twice must be a no-op the second time (verified by unit/integration tests).
- Reconciliation latency: importer applies a bundle and updates metrics within 30s for 99th percentile.

Security & compliance:
- Bundles are encrypted at rest on the collector and signed to detect tampering. Signatures are verified by the importer; failed verification moves bundle to quarantine.
- KMS integration required for node keys; default behavior uses EHSM on customer private deployment.
- Audit logs emitted for any conflict resolution operations.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for bundle serialization, sign/verify, and idempotent apply logic.
- Integration test harness that simulates intermittent uploads, retries, reorderings, and split-brain node failures.
- Load test using recorded production traces to verify bundle size and importer throughput.
- Canary rollout: start with low-traffic pilot customers (2 customers) for 2 weeks, then expand to 5, then broad rollout.

Migration/rollout notes:
- Collector supports both old "opaque" blobs and new compact bundles for a transition window (6 weeks). Collector will tag legacy exports with legacy_format=true so importer can route to legacy reconciliation flow.
- Provide a one-time migration tool to reprocess stored legacy blobs into compact bundles for customers that opt-in.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Manifest format: protobuf v2 vs JSON. Protobuf preferred for size but makes ad-hoc debugging harder; mitigated by sampled raw events.
- Sequence generation: use monotonic counter vs time-based monotonic token (risk of wrap). Decided to use 128-bit (node_id + monotonic counter) to avoid reuse.
- Local enforcement vs deferred enforcement: we keep local enforcement to preserve UX even when offline, at cost of reconciling rejects on cloud side.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TELEMETRY/Compact+Usage+Bundler+Design
- Proto schema (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/compact-bundler/protos/v1
- Importer POC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-telemetry/pull/128
- Test harness (k6 scripts): https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-load-tests

Rollout plan summary:
1) Merge collector + importer support behind feature flag.
2) Enable feature on 2 pilot customers (manual enable). Monitor reconciliation metrics and billing diffs.
3) Expand to 5 customers. Fix issues.
4) Enable default for new on-prem installs. Deprecate legacy blobs after 6 weeks.
